transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you for seeing me, Doctor. I... I suppose I'm here because of a little incident at work. It really wasn't a huge deal, just a minor lapse in judgment, but my team suggested I talk to someone, and I always want to do right by them. Is it alright if I explain what happened? 

I was on a board call recently, and someone asked a very simple, standard question about the facility budget. And, well... I snapped at them. I raised my voice, which I almost never do. It was just a moment of stress, you know? But it's not how I run my company, and it's certainly not how I treat people. I just want to make sure I'm handling things the right way, if that makes sense?
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Anxious? Oh, no, I wouldn't say anxious. I mean, maybe just a little keyed up, but that's normal for my line of work, right? You have to be a bit on your toes to keep things running smoothly. I certainly don't feel... out of control or anything like that. Just the usual day-to-day pressures. Does that sound like a reasonable way to feel, given the responsibilities I have?
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Sad? Oh, no, I wouldn't say sad. I have a good life, a great company... I have no reason to be down, really. 

I suppose... well, I want to be completely thorough for you, so I will say I've noticed things are just feeling a little... flat? Usually, if I need to settle my mind after a long day, I'll work on a chess problem, or maybe look through my old hiking notes, or just have a nice, quiet dinner with my wife. But lately, it's like I know I *should* be enjoying those things, but I just can't quite get there. 

It's just a bit dull right now, I guess. But that's probably just a normal reaction to being a little overworked, don't you think? It doesn't mean anything serious, right?
Have you lost interest in activities that you normally enjoy?

Well, I... I think I just mentioned that, didn't I? About the chess and the hiking notes? I mean, I wouldn't say I've *lost* interest, exactly. That sounds so... permanent, or like there's something wrong with me. 

I still do those things, I still sit down with the chessboard. It's just that the spark isn't quite there right this second. It's more of a temporary lull, I'm sure of it. Everyone goes through phases where their hobbies feel a bit like routine, wouldn't you agree? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so you have the full picture, but I really don't think it's anything to worry about.
Do you often find yourself worrying about being criticized or rejected by others?

Criticized or rejected? Oh, definitely not. No, I wouldn't say I worry about that at all. I mean, in my position, as a chief executive, you have to have a pretty thick skin, right? You make decisions, and people are going to have opinions. That's just the nature of the job.

I certainly don't sit around fretting over what people think of me. I try to be fair and do my best, and I think people respect that. It's important to project confidence, wouldn't you say? I really don't think I have any issues with worrying about rejection or anything like that. That's a sign of a healthy mindset, right?
Do you find yourself being overly perfectionistic or preoccupied with details at work or in your personal life?

Overly perfectionistic? Oh, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, obviously, when you're running a company, you... you want things done properly. You have to have standards. But preoccupied with details? No, I've always been more of a big-picture guy. 

You hire good people and let them handle the day-to-day minutiae, right? I think getting bogged down in every little thing just slows you down and frustrates everyone. I certainly don't obsess over things being absolutely flawless. I try to keep a very healthy, balanced perspective on things, both at the office and at home. That's really the best way to handle life, don't you think?
Do you often find yourself avoiding certain social interactions or relationships due to fear of being embarrassed or judged?

Avoid social interactions? No, no, I wouldn't say that at all. In my line of work, you... you really can't afford to hide from people, can you? I've always been quite comfortable in a room full of people. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I might skip a networking dinner or a gala, but that's just because it's been a long week and I'm tired. It's certainly not because I'm afraid of being embarrassed or judged. I've built my business and my life from the ground up, and I think people generally respect that. I don't really give them a reason to judge me anyway. I try to treat everyone well and hold my head high. That makes sense, doesn't it? You have to be out there and confident to get anywhere in life.
Do you find it difficult to delegate tasks to others?

Difficult to delegate? Oh, no, not at all. Actually, I'd say that's one of my strong suits. When you build a business from the ground up... well, you learn pretty quickly that you can't do every single thing yourself. You have to surround yourself with capable people and just let them do their jobs, right? 

I've got a fantastic team, and I trust them completely. I mean, sure, I like to be kept in the loop—any good boss would—but I certainly don't hover over their shoulders or hold onto tasks I shouldn't. Giving people responsibility is how you help them grow, wouldn't you agree? So, no, delegating is really not an issue for me. I think I handle that part of the job quite well.
Have you ever felt like you're having trouble controlling your temper in situations other than the incident at work?

Well, I wouldn't say I have trouble controlling my temper in general. I've always prided myself on being very level-headed, you know? You don't get to where I am by flying off the handle at every little thing. 

But... well, I suppose that is actually why I came in to see you. I... I had a bit of an uncharacteristic moment recently. We were on a board call, and someone asked a very minor question about the facility budget, and I just... I snapped at them. I really lost my cool over something so small. 

It was very out of character for me. That is absolutely not how I run my company, and it's certainly not how I treat my people. I've always believed in professional respect, right? So, having that happen... it bothered me enough to make this appointment. I just want to make sure I'm managing my stress the right way, you know? That makes sense to get checked out, doesn't it?
Have you had any other incidents similar to the one at work where you lost your temper?

Other incidents? Oh, no, absolutely not. I mean... no, nothing like that. Like I said, that kind of outburst is really not who I am. I've always been very careful to keep things professional, you know? 

It was just that one specific board call. I certainly haven't snapped at anyone at home or... or anywhere else. I think it was just a fluke, really. A momentary lapse because of how much I've had on my plate lately. You understand how that can happen to anyone, right? It was just the one bad moment, but otherwise, I'm completely back to my usual self. I'm doing the right thing by just checking in about it though, aren't I?
How long have you been feeling like things are a bit dull?

Well, I suppose it's been... maybe just since that board call, or right around then. It's really nothing major, I promise. I just mean... you know how you have those things that usually help you unwind? For me, it's working on a good chess problem, or going over my hiking notes, or just having a nice, quiet dinner with my wife. 

Lately, though... I don't know, they just feel a bit flat. Like, I know I should be enjoying them, and I want to, but I just can't quite get there right now. It's probably just normal fatigue, right? When you're running a company, sometimes you just get a little too drained to enjoy your hobbies for a week or two. That's pretty common for people in my position, wouldn't you say?
How long have you been feeling like things are a bit dull?

Well, let's see... I suppose it's been about six days now. Yes, right around six days. It started right after... well, right after that incident at the facility. We were doing a walkthrough and there was... an explosion and a fire. 

It was a very chaotic situation, as you can imagine, but we handled it. Everyone got out. But I think ever since then, things have just felt a little... muted. Like I said, it's really not a big deal, just a bit of a slump since the fire. It's completely normal to feel a little off for a few days after something like that, isn't it? I'm sure it'll pass in no time.
Have you felt this way of things being dull for most of the day, every day, since it started?

Oh, no, definitely not all day. I mean... I wouldn't say it's every single moment, no. 

When I'm at the office, I'm still... you know, I'm still very focused on what needs to be done. I wouldn't let myself just sit around feeling unmotivated all day, that's really not my style. It's more just... here and there. In the quiet moments, maybe, when I finally sit down. But it's certainly not a constant cloud over me or anything like that. 

I'm still functioning perfectly well and keeping on top of my responsibilities, which is the main thing, right? I figure since it's not happening all day long, it just means it's a passing phase. Wouldn't you agree?
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Guilty? Oh, no. No, I don't think so. I mean, obviously, as CEO, you always wonder if you could have... well, implemented a different safety protocol or checked a report twice. You know how it is, the buck stops with me. But actual guilt? No, I wouldn't say that. 

We had the best safety ratings in the sector, and I made sure my team followed every guideline to the letter. It was just a freak accident, really. Nobody blames me, and I certainly don't blame myself. It's just one of those unfortunate things that happens in industry sometimes, don't you think? You can't control every little variable, right?
Have you been feeling worthless or blaming yourself for anything lately?

Worthless? Oh, definitely not. No, I... I've built a very successful company from the ground up, you know? I know my value, and I know what I bring to the table. I'm still very much capable of leading my team. 

And as for blaming myself... well, like I was just saying, it was a freak accident. I mean, sure, I've had a few moments where I replay things, but that's just being thorough, isn't it? Making sure we learn from it. But I don't sit around feeling worthless or beating myself up. That wouldn't be very productive, would it? I think I'm handling it all quite reasonably, all things considered. Don't you?
Have you been feeling irritable most of the time since the incident at work?

Well... I wouldn't say *most* of the time. I'm usually very even-keeled. You have to be, in my position. But... I suppose I have had a moment or two where I was a bit shorter than usual. 

Actually, that's... that's sort of why I decided to come in and talk to someone. We had a board call recently, and... someone asked a very standard, minor question about the facility budget. And I just... I snapped at them. I raised my voice and was quite sharp. 

It really took me by surprise, to be honest. That is absolutely not how I run my company, and it's certainly not how I treat my people. I pride myself on being professional. So... yes, a little irritable in that one instance, but I'm sure it's just the stress of the situation, right? Anyone would be a little on edge after an incident like that, wouldn't they?
Have you been feeling irritable for more than half of the days since the incident at work?

More than half the days? Oh, no. No, certainly not. I mean, I'm a professional, you know? I can't afford to be snapping at people left and right, it just wouldn't do. 

Like I said, that board call was... well, it was an exception. An anomaly. Most days I'm perfectly fine, just handling business as usual. You have to keep a level head when you're steering the ship, and I think I do a rather good job of that, all things considered. It's just that one slip-up, really. That's not so bad, is it? I mean, given everything that's happened, keeping it together most days is... well, it's a good sign, isn't it?
Have you been feeling irritable for most of the day on most days since the incident at work?

Most of the day? Oh, definitely not. No, I... I think I'd have a mutiny on my hands if I were walking around barking at people all day long, you know? 

I really do try to keep a positive atmosphere at the office. Morale is so important, especially right now. So, no, I'm not sitting at my desk fuming from morning till night. That board meeting was just... a momentary lapse in judgment, a few minutes out of an otherwise perfectly normal week. 

I'm usually very good at leaving my stress at the door when I walk into the building. I mean, a leader has to project stability, right? And I think I've been doing a pretty decent job of that, don't you? Most of the time, I'm just my usual self.
Have you been feeling irritable nearly every day since the incident at work?

Every day? Oh, heavens no. I... I know I'm repeating myself a bit, doctor, but I really only came in to see you because of that one specific moment. You know, when I snapped on that board call over the little facility budget question. 

I just... I really need you to understand that is absolutely not how I run my company, and it's definitely not how I treat my people. If I were walking around irritable every single day, I wouldn't have a business left! I pride myself on being respectful and treating my employees right. So it really was just that one slip-up, I promise. That makes sense, right? I'm sure you see a lot of folks who just have one bad moment when they're under a lot of pressure?
Have you been feeling irritable every day since the incident at work?

Every day? No, no, absolutely not. I think... well, I know I've mentioned this already, but I really just came to see you because of that one specific incident. Snapping on that board call... just over a tiny question about the facility budget. It was so out of character for me. 

I just want to be sure you know that's not who I am. It's not how I run my company, and it's certainly not how I treat my people. If I were irritable every day, I wouldn't be much of a CEO, would I? It really was just that one bad moment. I'm sure you understand, right? People under stress sometimes just have one little crack, but it doesn't mean they're falling apart every single day.
